ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of shareholders, managers, UBOs and counterparties against the UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list for USD clearing counterparts, the Luxembourg national asset-freeze measures, and Interpol notices. Politically exposed persons are identified per Directive (EU) 2015/849 and the Law of 12 November 2004; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, including independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval for establishing or continuing the business relationship, and intensified monitoring of high-risk jurisdictions and complex ownership structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), via https://www.lbr.lu, with mandatory e-filing of name pre-validation and notarial direct access
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the operative filing language for RCS registrations and statutory documents; the corporate name must be composed in Latin script, may contain Luxembourgish, French, German or transliterated foreign elements, and must not be contrary to public order or good morals or be misleading. The legal-form suffix 'S.à r.l.' must be included in the registered name. Names in non-Latin scripts require transliteration into Latin characters and a certified French version.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (requires CSSF license and prior authorization)
SICAV / Fonds / OPCVM / FIA / Open-Ended Fund (reserved to CSSF-authorized undertakings)
AIFM / Gestionnaire de fonds d'alternatifs (reserved regulated title)
État / Ministère / Administration / Commune (suggesting public authority)
Trésorerie / Holding financier / Finance (requires justification and potential CSSF clearance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an RCS/LBR name rejection, the notary or applicant may resubmit a rectified or alternative name through the lbr.lu gateway, or file a reasoned administrative complaint with the Registrar of the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. If the adverse decision is maintained, annulment proceedings may be brought before the Tribunal administratif of Luxembourg within three months of notification. Parallel private-law remedies are available before the district courts in the event of third-party trademark or trade-name opposition.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Commercially domiciliated addresses are permissible for SARL registration under the Law of 31 May 1999 on company domiciliation, provided a real physical Luxembourg address is maintained where legal process and correspondence can be served. For the licensed multi-family office operating as a CSSF-supervised financial-sector professional, a pure letterbox or virtual arrangement is not admissible; management, compliance, internal control and risk-management functions must be physically established in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 70-85% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the CSSF within the first 24 months of operation for a licensed high-risk financial-sector professional, consistent with the CSSF risk-based supervisory cycle. Unannounced substance audits by the RCS and the Luxembourg direct tax administration may also occur, particularly under the OECD economic-substance and global minimum top-up tax frameworks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Companies Act of 10 August 1915, as amended, notably by the Law of 10 August 2016 on modernisation of company law) – SARL governed by Articles 710-1 to 710-22 (formation, minimum capital, gérance, shareholders' general meetings) and general formation provisions in Articles 1 to 3; Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector (Articles 24-28 applying to investment firms) governs the regulated multi-family office activity; Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions governs the Autorisation d'établissement.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 3, rue du Parc des Expositions, L-1113 Luxembourg; electronic filings through the e-RCS web portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif notarié (notarially executed deed of incorporation containing the French-language Articles of Association, 'Statuts') deposited with the RCS for immatriculation of the Luxembourg SARL.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 under Article 710-1 of the Companies Act of 10 August 1915. The SARL capital must be fully subscribed at formation; cash contributions must be released to at least 20% of the nominal value of the shares, although standard banking practice requires the full EUR 12,000 to be deposited into a blocked escrow current account ('compte bloqué') opened in the name of the company en formation at a Luxembourg credit institution. The bank's blocking certificate is remitted to the notary, and the funds are released to the company upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION PASSED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [MFO] SARL, A SOCIÉTÉ À RESPONSABILITÉ LIMITÉE INCORPORATED IN LUXEMBOURG. The founding shareholders unanimously resolve: (i) the share capital of EUR 12,000 has been fully subscribed; (ii) the registered office is fixed at [street address], L-[postal code], Luxembourg; (iii) Mr./Ms. [Name Surname] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole signature and full authority to represent the company; (iv) the Manager is authorised to open bank accounts, execute all notarial and RCS filings, and file the CSSF authorisation for discretionary portfolio management and investment advice; (v) no management remuneration is fixed for the first financial year.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name and Certificate of Non-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-RCS online counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online request for a 'certificat de non-immatriculation' to verify that the proposed name '[PROPOSED NAME] SARL' is not already used; obtain the RCS certificate evidencing availability of the name; concurrently instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the draft statutes and to conduct a trade-mark availability check against the Luxembourg and EU registers.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS name-reservation request form
Passport or national identity card of each founding shareholder
Proposed corporate name and brief statement of corporate object (ISIC 6430 / NAICS 523920)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name conflicts with an existing RCS registration, file an amended name containing distinguishing elements (e.g., 'MFO ADVISORY LUX SARL') and obtain a fresh certificate of non-registration; no formal opposition mechanism applies at RCS level.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of the French-language Articles of Association and CSSF Pre-consultation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notarial office (licensed civil-law notary) and external legal counsel on the Luxembourg bar; CSSF pre-gateway advice may be sought
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French containing the corporate object limited to multi-family office portfolio advisory services, registered office clause, EUR 12,000 share capital structure, gérant appointment mechanics, and statutory exclusions preserving the regulatory boundary; conduct a CSSF pre-filing consultation on the multi-family office business model to ensure the object clause aligns with the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector; obtain final counsel approval of the objet social.
required_dossiers: Detailed corporate-object description (ISIC 6430 / NAICS 523920)
Identities of all founding shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Draft French-language statutes with the prescribed mandatory clauses
CSSF preliminary written opinion or practitioner notes, if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the CSSF pre-filing response identifies an over-broad or ambiguous object, amend the statutory clause by adding or narrowing the reserved activities and resubmit the draft for notarial and regulatory review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Escrow Capital Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorised by the CSSF (e.g., BIL, Spuerkeess, BGL BNP Paribas or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked bank account in the name of the company 'en formation'; complete the bank's full KYC and AML/CFT documentation; deposit at least EUR 12,000 on behalf of the subscribers; obtain the bank's attestation de blocage de fonds (blocking certificate) confirming the amount held and the blocking conditions; the certificate will be presented to the notary at signing.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application completed by the authorised founder(s)
AML/KYC questionnaire on all shareholders and beneficial owners
Source of funds and source of wealth declarations with supporting evidence
Draft Articles of Association for the bank file
Identification documents and corporate documents of any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further documentation or declines the file, the founders must supplement the KYC submission or select an alternative Luxembourg credit institution; notarisation cannot proceed without a valid blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarised Execution of the Acte Constitutif
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public domiciled and practising in Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene all founding shareholders before the notary, either personally or by apostilled specific power of attorney; the notary verifies the bank blocking certificate, the subscription and payment statement, and the legality of the statutes; the founders sign the acte constitutif containing the statuts; the first gérant must accept office either in the deed or by a separate notarised acceptance, and the notary collects the fixed registration duty.
required_dossiers: Final French-language Articles of Association
Bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds)
Subscription and payment statement (état de souscription et de libération) signed by the founders
Apostilled notarial powers of attorney for any founder acting by proxy
UBO declaration forms and proof of no-discharge or good standing for corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a legal defect, the parties sign a curative rectification deed (acte rectificatif) before the same notary; the statutory one-month period for RCS deposit runs only from the perfected deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Immatriculation and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-RCS notarial filing module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarial deed and the RCS registration form electronically; the RCS verifies the deed's compliance with the Companies Act and registers the SARL; the company acquires legal personality on registration; the RCS issues the registration number (Numéro d'immatriculation 'B-XXXXXX') and an extract of the register evidencing incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
RCS registration request form duly completed
Bank capital deposit blocking certificate
Certificate of non-registration of the company name
Notarial identification sheet and powers for the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rectification request ('marge'), the notary files the corrected particulars within 15 days; if the one-month deposit deadline is missed, re-execution of the constitutive act before the notary is required before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Deed in the RESA Official Electronic Compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS publishes the constitutive deed and the mandatory particulars (company name, form, capital, registered office, gérant, object) in RESA, the official electronic compendium of companies; request the consolidated RCS extract with legal-personality mention and order the shareholders register book (registre des associés) to be maintained once physical premises are established.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Full text of the notarised Articles of Association for publication
List of legal representatives and their powers of representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any published particular is inaccurate, file a corrective publication (rectificatif) promptly through the RCS; the registry will republish the corrected data without material effect on legal personality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Shareholders' and Management Resolution, Governance Books and Registered-Office Formalisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and the appointed Gérant (internal corporate governance under Articles 710-1 to 710-22 of the 1915 Law)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first shareholders' meeting and approve the pro-forma first board resolution set out above; adopt the signed minutes (procès-verbal); obtain the gérant's signed acceptance of office; execute the registered-office consent letter from the landlord; establish the statutory books (minutes register, associates register, capital transactions register), the AML/CFT internal policy and the UBO register required under the Law of 13 January 2019 on the register of beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Draft pro-forma first board resolution
Signed minutes of the first shareholders' meeting
Consent to act and acceptance of office by the Gérant
Landlord's registered-office acceptance letter
AML/CFT internal policy and risk assessment manual
Beneficial owner filing sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any signature or consent is missing, obtain the omitted item within 48 hours; in an SARL, a unanimous written resolution in lieu of a physical meeting is permissible unless the statutes prescribe a notarial form.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD - Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for RCS company registration. Operational portals: myguichet.lu (e-RCS and eTVA electronic filing), guichet.lu (public administrative guide), and the ACD e-filing channel via mybusiness.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SARL and register in the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via e-RCS on myguichet.lu; the automatically attributed national business registration number (numéro d'identification / matricule) serves as the corporate TIN for direct tax purposes. 2) Register for VAT with the AED (format LU + 8 digits) using the standard electronic FEL registration form; non-resident taxable persons performing taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with the AED from the first euro, while resident SARLs register for VAT upon incorporation if taxable activity is expected. 3) The ACD opens the corporate income tax file automatically for resident companies upon RCS registration; no separate direct tax registration is required for a Luxembourg-resident SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the resident SARL is per se an opaque corporate taxpayer subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) on worldwide income and net wealth, with treaty and domestic relief for foreign-source income; no transparent or pass-through classification is available for a SARL under Luxembourg law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime. Elective mechanisms include: (a) tax consolidation (fiscal unity / intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for a Luxembourg-resident group of companies at least 95% owned by a common parent; (b) election to treat a foreign permanent establishment as a Luxembourg PE for treaty-attribution purposes under Article 48 LIR with an optional consistency election under ATAD 2; (c) a hybrid-alignment election under the Law of 21 December 2020 implementing ATAD 2 to recharacterise hybrid entities/instruments and avoid double non-taxation; (d) the VAT small-business exemption election under Article 57 of the VAT Law for annual turnover below EUR 35,000 (once elected, generally binding for a period).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended, implementing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business exemption (Article 57 VAT Law); no registration threshold applies to non-resident suppliers performing taxable supplies in Luxembourg, who must register from the first euro unless the supply is subject to reverse charge with a Luxembourg VAT-registered recipient; intra-EU distance-selling and OSS thresholds follow EU rules (EUR 10,000 cross-border intra-EU annual threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing (EN 16931 / PEPPOL-compliant) for domestic B2B transactions enters into force on 1 January 2026 under the Luxembourg e-invoicing reform, with sanctions phased from 2027. No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping/API clearance regime is currently implemented; VAT returns and recapitulative statements are filed electronically (eTVA) on a monthly, quarterly, or annual cycle with aggregate declaration data; invoice-level transaction reporting to the tax administration is not yet mandatory except for intra-EU EC Sales Lists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies on the dispatch/transport of goods to a non-EU destination provided the exporter retains full customs export evidence (SAD/ECS exit confirmation); domestic supplies to an export vendor or freight forwarder for subsequent export are exempt under Article 151 of the VAT Law. Services: cross-border B2B services supplied to a non-Luxembourg taxable person are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (reverse charge at 0% in the customer's jurisdiction), while B2C services to non-EU customers qualify for zero-rating when the effective use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU (Article 148 VAT Law). For an MFO SARL, discretionary portfolio advisory and management fees invoiced to a non-EU fund, family vehicle, or non-established investor will qualify for 0% where the place-of-supply rules locate the service abroad and the exporter holds adequate documentary proof of the customer's foreign establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ECS) with Movement Reference Number and customs exit confirmation
Transport document evidencing physical export: Bill of Lading (sea) or CMR/AWB (road/air)
Commercial invoice and underlying advisory or portfolio management contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of consideration from abroad
Proof of customer's non-Luxembourg establishment (foreign VAT registration certificate or official certificate of residence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT law requires strict documentary substantiation for zero-rated exports; if the export bundle is incomplete, the AED will reclassify the supply as taxable at 16% and claw back the VAT together with statutory late-payment interest of 0.8% per month, a 10% late-payment surcharge, and administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 per offence. Fraudulent zero-rating schemes or contrived export arrangements constitute tax fraud punishable by imprisonment (8 days to 5 years) and criminal fines, with the normal assessment period extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or wilful concealment; transfer-pricing and substance audits may further recharacterise long-outstanding unrepatriated export consideration as a deemed shareholder distribution or indirect capital contribution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); banking prudential and AML/KYC supervision: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). There is no separate Luxembourg foreign-exchange control authority; EU capital-movement liberalisation under Articles 63-66 TFEU applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg. Current-account items such as management fees, advisory fees, interest, salaries, custody fees, and dividend payments are freely payable. Capital-account items such as equity injections, shareholder loans, portfolio transfers, and direct investments require no BCL authorisation. Profit remittance is not foreign-exchange blocked; the practical hurdles are documentary and tax-related: banks require evidence of source of funds, economic substance, valid shareholder resolutions, tax residence certificates, and CSSF compliance. Dividend distributions may be subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at 15% domestic rate, 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when conditions are satisfied, or reduced under double-taxation treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion into euro, and no repatriation deadline. Export receipts, fee income, or advisory proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the market rate through a licensed credit institution. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL may be required, and all cross-border transfers remain subject to standard AML/CFT controls.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for truly offshore digital EMIs; MEDIUM only for EEA-licensed electronic money institutions that validly passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and the EU Electronic Money Directive. A non-EEA EMI cannot lawfully provide principal corporate treasury services to a Luxembourg SARL, and funds held with an unregulated offshore EMI will not satisfy the blocked-capital verification required by a Luxembourg notary for an SARL capital escrow. Any permitted EMI must be supervised in an EEA state, passported to Luxembourg, maintain safeguarding of client funds, settle through Target2 or SEPA, and submit to equivalent KYC/AML diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the amended Luxembourg AML law require robust customer due diligence but do not impose a universal statutory requirement for physical presence. In practice, however, tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one organisational KYC interview with directors and UBOs, and most will mandate a physical meeting at the bank or before a Luxembourg notary/lawyer for a high-risk multi-family office. Remote or hybrid onboarding is occasionally accepted when the client is a low-risk corporate, but for an ISIC 6430 multi-family office the prevailing policy is physical presence for the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner, supported by eIDAS-compliant electronic signatures, apostilled documentation, banker references, and notarised corporate extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client classified as High-Risk Special-License entity: multi-family office with discretionary portfolio advisory under ISIC 6430 / NAICS 523920
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF licence or no-objection confirmation; full regulatory business plan; internal AML/CFT procedures manual; professional indemnity insurance; organisational chart; outsourcing agreements; audited or reviewed annual accounts; tax status evidence; written confirmation that the SARL does not operate as an unlicensed payment institution, trust company, or custodian.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity through trust layers, SPVs, nominee shareholders, or family-governance structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); full holding-chain diagram from the SARL to all natural-person UBOs; passports and proof of residential address; trust deeds or family constitution documents; statutory minutes appointing directors; legal opinion confirming absence of bearer shares or nominee concealment; CRS/FATCA registration evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth or source of funds for equity injections and shareholder loans, particularly from non-EU jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: At least 12-24 months of personal and corporate bank statements; independent source-of-wealth letters; sale, inheritance, gift, or remuneration documentation; shareholder loan agreements compliant with Luxembourg transfer-pricing principles; tax returns and tax-residence certificates; notarised certificates; SWIFT payment records; written commercial rationale for the Luxembourg treasury structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status, sanctions-list hits, adverse media, or exposure to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP/sanctions/adverse-media questionnaires; negative screening results from a regulated compliance data provider; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds dossier; citizenship and residence permits; clean criminal records certificates; independent legal opinion; enhanced monitoring undertaking and commitment to provide periodic transaction and position statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose mismatch: a small SARL managing significant family assets but lacking Luxembourg substance, a professional licence, or a clear payment-activity narrative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF authorisation and MiFID portfolio-management records; physical substance documentation such as lease, payroll, and Luxembourg management arrangements; service contracts with client families; RCS extract defining authorised corporate purpose; prohibition on routing third-party non-investment payments; evidence that all outbound payments are investment-related and subject to internal escalation and monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital injections must be routed through a Luxembourg or EU-regulated credit institution. For initial SARL capital, transfer funds to a blocked 'société en formation' account at a tier-1 Luxembourg bank; the bank issues a blocked-funds certificate to the notary; after notarial deed execution and RCS registration, funds are released to the operational account. For subsequent equity or shareholder-loan injections, use SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the EEA, with ISO 20022 structured remittance and a purpose description such as 'Share capital contribution' or 'Shareholder loan disbursement'; where the receiving bank requires a Luxembourg balance-of-payments code, the bank will map the transaction to direct-investment capital categories. Verification package: notarially certified shareholders' resolutions; updated RCS and RBE filings; source-of-funds evidence; prior share-subscription statements; transfer-pricing documentation for interest-bearing shareholder loans; and no further BCL approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT gpi customer credit transfers via MT103, together with MT202 COV for interbank cover, for non-EEA payments in any convertible currency; SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for euro disbursements within the EEA; commercial letters of credit issued by SWIFT MT700 and governed by UCP600, with MT707 amendments and MT752 reimbursement instructions; documentary collections using MT400/MT410 when no LC is required. All euro leg settlements ultimately clear through TARGET2 or commercial-bank money with final settlement under Luxembourg law and EU Regulation 260/2012. Payments are subject to sanctions screening, adverse-media filtering, CSSF transaction-monitoring, and escalation for any high-risk clearing jurisdiction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright over-the-counter FX forwards against EUR under standard ISDA 1998 FX Definitions, used for hedging operational currency exposure only
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with offshore convertibility restrictions, executed through a licensed Luxembourg or EU bank
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term balance-sheet hedging between EUR and USD, GBP, or CHF, subject to EMIR clearing and margining obligations where applicable
FX swaps and roll-over swaps for short-term treasury liquidity conversion without creating speculative open positions
Vanilla FX call and put options under MiFID-II suitability and derivatives governance, provided the MFO investment mandate permits option premiums
Exchange-traded FX futures cleared through regulated CCPs for highly liquid currency pairs when authorised by the investment policy and risk committee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (comptes annuels) with the Register of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year (balance sheet date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to EUR 5,000; possible judicial strike-off or administrative dissolution in case of persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following each annual LBR reminder (or within 30 days after any shareholding transfer); anniversary-based calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors subject to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment; default may trigger administrative deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for a SARL exceeding two of three criteria: balance-sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average workforce > 50 FTE. CSSF-supervised entities (e.g., licensed multi-family offices) require a statutory audit irrespective of thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 23 September 2011); IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts of subsidiary groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every calendar year, the SARL must file a written confirmation with the RBE stating the existing beneficial owners, following the LBR annual reminder. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be confirmed within one month to update the register.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City; cumulative corporate income tax 17% + 7% solidarity surcharge = 18.19%, plus municipal business tax 6.75% on deductible base; rates vary by municipality)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP tax regime (80% exemption of qualifying IP net income, effective rate 5.2%); notional interest deduction (NID) granting a deductibility of notional interest on real equity increases; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (0% WHT and 0% CIT on exempts)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (subject to anti-abuse rules for change of activity/ownership; no carryback)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 6 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via the eTax portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD), accessible through MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the return must be filed by 30 June of the following year; for off-calendar fiscal years, within 6 months after the fiscal year-end. Extensions (e.g., to 31 December) may be granted upon formal request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Luxembourg RCS registration number (B number), registered office address, and tax payer identification number (TIN)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the local tax registration number issued by the ACD and the Luxembourg fiscal agent contact details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal economic activity code (NACE/ICN), which must correspond to the actual business scope; for the subject entity: NACE 64.30 (Activities of holding companies) and secondary code 66.30 (Portfolio management) or 70.22 (Business consultancy) as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the NACE/ICN code that accurately reflects the discretionary portfolio advisory service; do not use a generic holding code if actual activity is custody/asset administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit after financial statement adjustments, add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., excess interest, taxes on income, fines), deduction of exempt income (participation, IP regime) and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report on a Luxembourg-book basis; maintain transfer pricing documentation for intra-group services and financing; include any arm’s-length adjustments required for direct/indirect cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying shareholding details (holding percentage, holding period, and source dividends or capital gains) to claim the exemption under Luxembourg law; attach a computation of exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that the non-resident shareholder qualifies under the 10% shareholding threshold and 12-month holding condition; a TC/TRC may be needed for reduced statutory rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity and IP box deduction (80% exemption on qualifying net IP income); also any foreign tax credits for withholding taxes suffered abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a separate NID/IP schedule with substantiation of the IP assets and income streams; NID can reduce CIT but does not affect municipal business tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable base, application of corporate income tax (17%), solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT), and municipal business tax (MBT, 6.75% in Luxembourg City) to derive the total assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity has any cross-border interest/royalty/dividend WHT, attach the repayment/refund forms to avoid double taxation; provide the ACD with proof of payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic penalty of 10% of the tax due, plus EUR 50–250 administrative fine; late payment: interest at 0.5% per month (6% p.a.) on underpaid tax from the due date until payment; willful omission or misrepresentation may escalate to tax fraud sanctions and possible criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (domestic rate; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when parent holds ≥10% for ≥12 months; treaty relief may reduce to 5% or 10% for direct shareholdings below 10%; a standard 0% is available for distributions to qualifying Luxembourg resident corporate shareholders)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke relief at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) provide the payer a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) for the fiscal year of payment, (ii) submit the Luxembourg ACD refund/relief request form (Form 76 – Exemption from withholding tax) together with a declaration of beneficial ownership, and (iii) for post-payment relief, file a refund claim with the ACD within five years of the payment date; the payer is not required to withhold if the TRC and form are provided before payment; anti-abuse (e.g., SCA 2.14 / EU ATAD) must be checked for treaty shopping
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties paid to non-residents, provided the payments are at arm’s length and not in the nature of hidden profit distributions; under Luxembourg’s tax treaties, interest typically attracts 0% and royalties 0–5% subject to beneficial ownership and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required where (a) the Luxembourg entity’s gross annual turnover exceeds EUR 10 million (Local File) and (b) the group’s consolidated annual turnover exceeds EUR 50 million (Master File); the Luxembourg entity must also submit a CbC Report if the group’s consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750 million; document acquisition, financing, IP, and management services with OECD-aligned functional and risk analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are applicable to Luxembourg entities performing core income-generating activities (including holding, financing, and intellectual property exploitation). A Multi-Family Office providing discretion portfolio advice must evidence: (i) local senior management and decision-making, (ii) adequate and proportioned staff, board meetings, and physical offices, (iii) active control of principal risks and core profit-generating assets; failure to substantiate economic substance exposes the entity to recharacterization of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, and sanctions under EU/OFAC/ATAD rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting taxable income, inflating deductions, falsifying books, or filing misleading tax returns; also misuse of shell structures to hide beneficial ownership (violating Luxembourg tax law and CFC/ATAD rules).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 plus interest (0.5%/month); criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment up to 5 years and disqualification from holding public office; the tax assessor can also reassess within 10 years in the case of fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to pay unpaid corporate taxes if they knowingly permit false filings; civil restitution of misappropriated assets, travel bans, and extradition risks arise under joint criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SARL with no local office, employees, books, or decision-making, especially when used for unilateral cross-border payment flows without business rationale; the ACD may apply the 'substance test' under the 2021 Luxembourg transparency law to treat the company as a non-resident for tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the entity as tax-transparent; denial of participation exemption, NID, and treaty relief; retroactive corporate income tax of 24.94% plus municipal business tax, 15% dividend WHT, penalties up to EUR 1,250 per infraction, and possible suspension of the business license for the regulated multi-family office activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face separate liability for penalties and interest; under the CSSF supervisory framework, failure to enforce substance may lead to withdrawal of the professional license and personal bans on holding a management position in a regulated entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence, PEP screening, or reporting suspicious activity under Luxembourg’s AML/CFT law (Law of 12 November 2004, amended); functioning as an unregistered investment manager or facilitating undisclosed beneficial ownership is an aggravating factor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative (CSSF) fine up to EUR 1 million or 10% of annual turnover, whichever higher; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000; imprisonment up to 5 years for willful money laundering; freezing of assets and revocation of the statutory license of the MFO.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for negligence; they may be prohibited from exercising roles in financial institutions; travel bans are imposed pending criminal investigation; civil liability for restitution of laundered funds is joint and several.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Adjustment and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intra-group service fees, loans, or IP royalties outside the arm’s length range without contemporaneous documentation; lending at excessive interest rates that shift profit out of Luxembourg; failing to satisfy the EU Interest Limitation Rule (30% EBITDA cap) and the Luxembourg ‘substance for financing’ requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority recharacterizes the transaction, adds back excessive deductions, calculates additional CIT and MBT at standard rates, imposes 10% late-filing penalty and 0.5% monthly interest; penalties may be doubled if no documentation is produced; the company is additionally exposed to CbC reporting non-compliance penalties up to EUR 4,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm’s length agreements may be jointly liable for the shortfall in corporate taxes; courts may apply the 'alter ego' doctrine to pierce the veil if funds are drained to related parties without consideration, leading to personal asset seizure and restraint orders.
